title: BBMRI MEMPRAGE — basal ganglia anatomy
clinicalHistory: Anonymized BBMRI volunteer MEMPRAGE — no acute presentation. Use this case to rehearse deep gray-matter anatomy on high-resolution T1.
technique: MEMPRAGE 1 mm isotropic sagittal (BBMRI-ERIC volunteer dataset).
learningObjectives: Identify caudate, putamen, and internal capsule on sagittal MEMPRAGE.
Relate deep gray-matter morphology to the frontal horn contour.
Describe a concise search pattern for basal ganglia on T1.
discussion: The BBMRI-ERIC sample is widely used for method development; here it anchors registrar anatomy before pathology cases. Requires the study in Orthanc (same UIDs as the FlowRad recording demo).
references: BBMRI-ERIC — European research biobank imaging resource.

findings.label: Caudate head
findings.description: The caudate head bulges into the frontal horn, forming the lateral wall of the ventricle on sagittal MEMPRAGE.
teachingPoints: Follow the caudate contour from head toward the body.
Compare left and right symmetry before calling subtle atrophy.

findings.label: Putamen
findings.description: Lentiform nucleus — putamen lies lateral to the internal capsule with slightly lower signal than globus pallidus externally.
teachingPoints: Trace internal capsule as the thin white-matter stripe between caudate and putamen.
Name structures aloud while scrolling — it trains report language.

findings.label: Frontal horn
findings.description: Use the frontal horn as your anchor — caudate head, corpus callosum genu, and septum pellucidum define this compartment.
teachingPoints: Ventricular shape changes quickly on sagittal scroll — pause each slice.
Link ventricular contour to adjacent parenchymal findings in reports.
